title: FLORA CITY COUNCIL MEETS
full_story:
The Flora City Council met Monday afternoon with Commissioner Lacey Lewis serving as Mayor Pro Tem in the absence of Mayor Linda Spicer.

Lewis opened the floor to public comment and Flora High School Student Athlete Gage Dugan addressed members about his new mentoring program called Upperclass Allies. As his mother Kendra Briscoe and grandfather Mike Briscoe looked on, Dugan explained the program’s intent is to pair Senior students with Junior High students who may have self-esteem issues, are a victim of bullying or may come from a non-traditional family. The goal is for the older students to impart a positive, consistent support system for those kids. To help the effort get underway, Upperclass Allies plans a fundraising event on Sunday August 16 from 3:00-7:00pm at Flora’s Library Park. It will serve as a Meet the Fall Athletes and Media Night to bring the community together and support students and the program. They plan to serve porkburgers, hot dogs, chips and drinks for those who attend. City Clerk Kaci O’Dell asked about providing insurance Kendra Briscoe stated that North Wayne Insurance is providing the coverage the group needs. Commissioners approved Dugan’s request unanimously.

Colin Mosely also addressed the council briefly. He stated that in his role as a volunteer first responder he has seen several recent accidents involving E-bikes or scooters. He said that while they love to see kids and others outside, he encouraged everyone to be careful and keep safety at the forefront of their mind. That message goes not only to riders but to vehicle drivers too. He urged both groups to be aware of others using the roads. He also stressed the importance of wearing safety gear, especially helmets.

Commissioner Lewis thanked him for his comments and Flora Police Chief Jeremy Ruger further emphasized the importance of wearing a helmet while operating one of these conveyances. Ruger also said that the Clay County Health Department is planning to offer E-bike/scooter safety classes in the near future.

Before moving on, Jacob Pharris addressed the council about the use of the Gazebo at Library Park for a wedding at the end of the month. He requests to use the park for an hour the evening of Friday, July 31 and again at Noon on Saturday, August 1. Clerk O’Dell told him about the insurance coverage needed and contingent on proof of insurance, commissioners approved his request without dissent.

Members voted to approve the meeting agenda and consent agenda, the latter including past meeting minutes, the Police Activity Report, the Building and Zoning Report, the Treasurers Report and the Warrant List for the first half of July.

Mayor Pro Tem Lewis next polled commissioners for their comments. Jeremy Henderson asked Mike Stanford about any news on the Downtown Grant that are used to assist local businesses. Stanford said he had checked with their contact and believes it is clearing the first hurdle, but another round of approval lies ahead, and the process is moving forward. Henderson asked if there was any timeline mentioned and Stanford responded that they won’t give a timeline.

Commissioner Phil Wiley took a moment to thank NAL for providing free swims for the public all summer long on Sundays. He reminds parents and students that Flora First Christian Church is hosting a school supply and bookbag giveaway this Wednesday from Noon to 5:00 and its open to those who need it in Clay County. Just stop in and pick out what is needed. He also called attention to the American Red Cross warning that the blood supply is dangerously low and encourages those who are able to give blood. The next drive is Friday from 1:00-5:00pm at the Flora Oddfellows Lodge, Caddy-cornered from the Post Office on East North Avenue. Wiley also mentioned the 4-H BBQ and Crain-Scates Bucking Bulls Rodeo this Friday, as the Clay County Fair gets underway. Finally, he encouraged people to see the good of living in a small rural community and remind others of it too.

City Administrator/Economic Development Director Mike Stanford presented three action items. He said Kieffer Brothers Construction is decreasing the cost of the Safe Routes to School by $2,565 thanks to using a less expensive style of drain systems in certain areas. Commissioners approved the change order. Members then approved an ordinance that ratifies a façade improvement grant for Stephen Hough at the Pit Stop Car Wash on W. North Avenue in the amount of $4,703. It will include new signage and other improvements. Stanford then moved on to a request to waive the formal bidding process for the replacement of a 6-inch high pressure main gas line and adds this is considered an emergency repair. He explained that during the replacement of the bridge over Raccoon Creek on Old Rt. 50 west of Charley Brown Park, worker discovered the high pressure line is exposed and is bowed, when it is supposed to be under the creek bed. The repair is to be completed by USDI of Olney with an estimated cost of between $116,500 and $141,751. Stanford says the 6-inch line is in the supply chain and is expected in about three weeks. He adds the 600 foot section will be installed without a service disruption. It should take about three days to complete it once they get started.

Flora City Treasurer Stephanie Bailey reminded city leaders that the city is preparing to move from server base storage to the cloud. When they do that July 27 or 28, service will be down primarily in the morning.

Building and Zoning Official Chad Bayles presented three action items. First, was an ordinance granting a variance to Amy Lee Realty at 201 E. 2nd St for a construction expansion. Commissioners approved her request and also approved the proposed ordinance granting special use for the addition of retail space at the same location. Bayles then presented an ordinance to grant a variance to Bill and Chris Thompson at 601 Douglas to build a privacy fence in their front yard on a corner lot. The variance was granted unanimously. Bayles closed by announcing that he had received call from someone reminding people that when you exercise your dog on a neighborhood walk, to please clean up afterwards. With all business complete, the meeting adjourned.

title: FLORA SCHOOL BOARD
full_story:
The Flora School Board met in regular session last night, approving the revisions to the Employee Handbook and the renewal of the E-Learning plan.

Superintendent Joel Hackney informed board members that online registration for the coming school year is being done through the Infinite Campus Portal.  In-person registration can be done at the building the child will attend on August 5th from 9:00 am to 3:00 pm.  Teacher Institute on August 11th, 12th, and 13th with first student attendance day on August 14th.

The board approved volunteer coaches for the 2026-2027 school year, and employed Leslie Bowling as special education teacher, contingent on obtaining proper licensure, Stacie Frech as part-time FACS/Art teacher, contingent on obtaining proper licensure, Whitney Cox as special education teacher, contingent on obtaining proper licensure, Alexis Williams as special education teacher, contingent on obtaining proper licensure, Angela Vincent as art teacher, contingent on obtaining proper licensure and Guy Durre as transportation secretary.  They also approved Alyssa Young as 7th grade girls basketball coach, and Jesse Campos as the JH softball coach.  They employed Jesse McCammon as school bus driver and Katie Berner as full-time transportation aide substitute and acknowledged receipt of the FMLA request for Dirk Hockman from September 14th through September 23rd.

title: CLAY COUNTY SHERRIF’S REPORT
full_story:
On Friday, the Clay County Sheriff’s Office assisted the US Marshal’s Service with the apprehension of a subject with an outstanding Federal Arrest Warrant.  Robert R. Shipley, 45, of Louisville, was arrested for Supervised Release Violation Petition on the original charge of Distribution of Child Pornography and Possession of Child Pornography.

On Sunday, July 12th, the Clay County Sheriff’s Office began an investigation into an individual who is subject to the Sex Offender Registration Act and was believed to be in non-compliance.  The sheriff’s office forwarded the investigation to the Clay County State’s Attorney’s Office and requested a warrant for the individual.

As a result of the investigation a warrant was issued for Michael W. Persinger Jr, 44, of Flora, for the offense of Unlawful Failure of Sex Offender to Notify.  On Friday, the Clay County Sheriff’s Office, Flora Police Department and US Marshal Service arrested Persinger on the warrant.  Persinger was transported to the Clay County Jail.

On Monday, Persinger appeared in Clay County Court and was granted Pretrial Release under the “Safe-T Act”.

The charges is merely an accusation and the defendant is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

title: HYDRANT FLUSHING
full_story:
The Village of Clay City will be flushing fire hydrants Thursday and Friday from 8 am to 3 pm.

Residents are warned that hydrant flushing may cause some water discoloration.  If you notice discoloration, run the spigot on the outside of your house for a few minutes and then run your cold water inside your home until it clears up.  Discolored water is safe, despite looking unusual, though it can stain white clothing if you are doing laundry.

title: FLORA POLICE ACTIVITY REPORT
full_story:
Flora Chief of Jeremy Ruger released his Activity Report for June during Monday’s Flora City Council meeting.

During the month, Flora police officers investigated six traffic accidents.

They made five criminal arrests.  There was one drug arrest and one DUI arrests during June.  There was one local ordinance arrests, 11 traffic arrests and three warrant arrests.

Officers issued 50 warning tickets, responded to 14 alarms and had 1,047 calls for service and had one juvenile contact.

Also, Flora police officers drove 5,143 miles and conducted 48 investigations during June.  They answered 324, 911 calls and conducted 12 UTV Inspections and no Golf Cart Inspections during June.

title: FLORA BUILDING AND ZONING REPORT
full_story:
Flora Building and Zoning Official Chad Bayles presented the monthly building and zoning report for June during Monday’s Flora City Council meeting.

The report shows eight new residential construction projects were undertaken in June, including four fences, three pools and one miscellaneous project with the total valued at $54,100.

And there were no new industrial projects started during June.

There were eight total new projects in Flora for June, valued at $54,100.

The year-to-date figures show 39 total residential projects so far this year with a value of $585,120.

There are four year-to-date commercial projects valued at $17,444,334 and no industrial projects.

That makes 43 total projects valued at $18,029,454, with $2,623 in permit fees and $600 in deposit fees collected for the year.

title: FRIENDS OF THE LIBRARY FALL BOOK SALE
full_story:
The Friends of the Flora Public Library Fall Book Sale will be held on Saturday, September 12th from 8 am to 3 pm.

Anyone wishing to contribute to the book sale can bring books that are in good shape to the front desk.  The Flora Public Library is open Monday through Thursday 1:00 – 8:00 pm, Friday 10:00 am to 6:00 pm and Saturday 10:00 am to 3:00 pm.  The library has a handcart to assist individuals who may be bringing a large volume of materials in.

The day of the sale all books, DVD’s and CD’s will be .25 cents.  Magazines are 10 cents each or 12 for $1.

title: COVER CROP FIELD DAY
full_story:
The Wayne County Soil and Water Conservation District is hosting a Cover Crop Field Day on Tuesday, August 18th at 4 pm at the Greg Dickey Farm in Wayne City.

Speakers will be David Kleinschmidt from Progressive Agronomy Consulting LLC,Torey Colburn from American Farmland Trust, and Dave Severin from the Illinois House of Representative.  There will be in field demonstrations, comparisons and a Soil Pit.

There will also be a meal for participants catered by Randy’s Smokehouse in Wayne City.  The Cover Crop Field Day is sponsored by the American Farmland Trust, Peoples National Bank and Farm Credit.

The Greg Dickey farm is located at 981 County Road 530, Wayne City, for more information call 618-842-7602 Ext 3.

title: WALK IN WEDNESDAYS RETURN
full_story:
Frontier Community College is once again opening its doors for Walk-In Wednesdays this month, offering prospective and current students a convenient way to get ready for the fall semester without the need for an appointment.

The next walk-in Wednesday is tomorrow from 9 am to 3 pm.  The last Walk-In Wednesdays will take place on 29th from 9 am to 3 pm.

The events are designed to streamline the enrollment process by providing one-stop access to key student services, including advising, class registration, financial aid assistance, and placement testing.  Staff will be on hand to answer questions and help students through each step.

To make the most of their visit, students are encouraged to bring their high school or college transcripts, a driver’s license or state ID, their Social Security number or card, and a completed FAFSA.  If applicable, students may also bring an IEP or 504 plan to help with academic accommodations.

More information is available by contacting FCC or visiting iecc.edu.
